scale: Sheets are @2x. 1x/ holds the same files at world px. Coordinates are px from the cell top-left (anchors) or from the anchor (offsets), screen y down.
camera: Same 3/4 map camera as towers-aim-v1 (35 deg elevation; ground circles squash to about 0.58 vertically). The drone was rendered in 3D at that camera, so every heading is a true view, not a rotated copy.

headings.order: index 0 = N (screen up), then clockwise: 1 = NNE, 4 = E (screen right), 8 = S (toward camera), 12 = W
headings.pick: i = round(atan2(dx, -dy) / 22.5deg) mod 16, where (dx, dy) is the drone's screen velocity (y down). Same rule as the towers, at 16 steps.
headings.bankNote: Each heading has a baked forward tilt (nose down 9 deg). There is no baked bank: for turns, rotate the drone sprite about its anchor by up to +/-6 deg, leaning into the turn (the preview uses bank = clamp(-yawRateDegPerSec * 0.06, -6, 6), eased). Do not rotate the shadow.

drone.layout: rows = 16 headings (row i = heading i), columns = 3 rotor-blur frames
drone.frameRect2x: x = frame * 140, y = heading * 100, w = 140, h = 100
drone.anchorMeaning: centre of the drone body. Draw it at (x, groundY - altitude). The anchor is the same point in every heading, so turning never makes it jump.
drone.dropOffsetMeaning: bomb release point (belly, under the camera pod) from the drone anchor, per heading. Spawn the bomb here.
drone.dropGroundMeaning: where a bomb released from that heading lands, from the drone's ground point (x, groundY). Same x as dropOffset; the bomb falls straight down on screen.

droneShadow.layout: one frame per heading, left to right, same index as the drone rows
droneShadow.anchorMeaning: ground point straight under the drone anchor: (x, groundY). Ground layer. Use the same heading index as the drone. Alpha is already about 40 percent at the centre; scale it if you want a lighter or darker shadow.
droneShadow.fallback: one round shadow: draw frame 0 or a 60 x 24 (@2x) soft ellipse if you prefer not to swap shadows.

bomb.anchorMeaning: centre of the bomb. Spawn with anchor = drone anchor + dropOffset + spawnOffset (the bomb top then sits on the release point).
bomb.note: Frame 1 has the cyan arming band lit, and the two frames rock +/-7 deg. The bomb is the same for every heading (it falls nose down). Explode when the nose (anchor + noseOffset) reaches the landing groundY.

bombShadow.note: At the landing point on the ground layer, scale from 0.4 to 1.0 and alpha from 0.45 to 1.0 over the fall.

explosion.note: Frames: 0 flash, 1 fireball (apply damage or slow here; shake the camera), 2 fireball breaking into smoke with the dust ring starting, 3-4 dust ring reaches the full radius, 5-7 smoke column rises and fades, ring thins out. No gore. The cell is wider than v1 (528 x 488 vs 432 x 432) and the anchor moved to match; the radius is the same. To match another radius, scale by radiusWorld / 92 about the anchor.

scorch.note: Ground decal centred on the impact. Frame 0 has glowing embers (show it for about 1 s), frame 1 is plain. Fade with alpha (see the README timeline). Same cell and anchor as v1.

events: drone enters on its path; pick the heading from velocity every frame
the landing point (drone ground point + dropGround[heading]) is over the target: spawn the bomb at the drop point; the drone keeps flying and turning
bomb nose reaches the ground: explosion frame 0, scorch (embers) on frame 1
explosion frame 1: apply the Drone Strike effect, shake the camera for about 0.15 s
scorch switches to the plain frame

changesFromV1: drone: 16 rendered headings x 3 rotor frames (v1 was one east-facing row)
droneShadow: one per heading (v1 had one)
drone cell 140 x 100 (v1 120 x 100), new anchor
dropOffset is per heading; dropGround is new
bomb cell 56 x 80 (v1 44 x 60), new anchor and offsets
explosion cell 528 x 488 (v1 432 x 432), new anchor, same radius
